records.literal_gloss: And was [the] ark of Yahweh in [the] territory of [the] Philistines seven months.

en.L: And the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was in the territory of [the] Philistines seven months.
en.B: The ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was in the land of the Philistines for seven months.
en.R: The ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stayed in Philistine territory for seven months.

es.L: Y el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} estuvo en el territorio de [los] filisteos siete meses.
es.B: El arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} estuvo en la tierra de los filisteos durante siete meses.
es.R: El arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se quedó en territorio filisteo durante siete meses.

fr.L: Et l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut dans le territoire des Philistins sept mois.
fr.B: L’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} resta sept mois dans le pays des Philistins.
fr.R: L’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est restée sept mois dans le territoire des Philistins.

sw.L: Na sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilikuwa katika eneo la Wafilisti miezi saba.
sw.B: Sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilikaa katika nchi ya Wafilisti kwa miezi saba.
sw.R: Sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilibaki katika nchi ya Wafilisti kwa miezi saba.

vi.L: Hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở trong lãnh thổ [của] người Phi-li-tin bảy tháng.
vi.B: Hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở trong xứ Phi-li-tin bảy tháng.
vi.R: Hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở lại trong lãnh thổ Phi-li-tin suốt bảy tháng.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 궤가 블레셋 사람들의 지역에 일곱 달 동안 있었다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 궤는 일곱 달 동안 블레셋 사람들의 땅에 있었다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 궤는 일곱 달 동안 블레셋 땅에 머물렀다.

pt.L: E a arca {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} esteve no território [dos] filisteus sete meses.
pt.B: A arca {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} ficou na terra dos filisteus durante sete meses.
pt.R: A arca {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} ficou no território dos filisteus por sete meses.

am.L: {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ታቦትም በፍልስጥኤማውያን አገር ሰባት ወር ነበረ።
am.B: {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ታቦት በፍልስጥኤማውያን ምድር ሰባት ወር ቆየ።
am.R: {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ታቦት በፍልስጥኤማውያን አገር ሰባት ወር ተቀመጠ።

decisions.choice: the ark of Yahweh: the chest that stood for Yahweh's presence, captured by the Philistines
decisions.reason: The Philistines had taken the ark in battle (4:11) and moved it from Ashdod to Gath to Ekron, and each city was struck with a plague (5:1-12). This chapter tells how they sent it back.

decisions.choice: territory of the Philistines: the whole Philistine country, not only open fields
decisions.reason: The word usually means "field", but it can name the open country or region belonging to a people (Genesis 32:4; Ruth 1:1). The ark had been in several Philistine cities, so the region as a whole is meant.

decisions.choice: the land of the Philistines (Balanced); Philistine territory (Readable)
decisions.reason: Both say plainly that the region is meant, not farmland.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic of 1 Samuel 6.
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change in Amharic.

source.text: וַיִּקְרְא֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים לַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים וְלַקֹּֽסְמִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מַֽה־נַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה לַאֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֑ה הוֹדִעֻ֕נוּ בַּמֶּ֖ה נְשַׁלְּחֶ֥נּוּ לִמְקוֹמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And called [the] Philistines for the priests and for the diviners, saying, What shall we do with [the] ark of Yahweh? Make known to us with what we shall send it to its place.

en.L: And [the] Philistines called for the priests and for the diviners, saying, "What shall we do with the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? Make known to us with what we shall send it to its place."
en.B: Then the Philistines summoned the priests and the diviners and said, "What should we do with the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? Tell us what we should send with it when we send it back to its place."
en.R: Then the Philistines called for their priests and for the men who claimed to learn hidden things from signs. They asked, "What should we do with the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? Tell us what we should send along with it when we send it back to where it belongs."

es.L: Y [los] filisteos llamaron a los sacerdotes y a los adivinos, diciendo: «¿Qué haremos con el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}? {{plural_you:Hágannos|Hacednos}} saber con qué la enviaremos a su lugar».
es.B: Entonces los filisteos convocaron a los sacerdotes y a los adivinos y les dijeron: «¿Qué debemos hacer con el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}? {{plural_you:Dígannos|Decidnos}} qué debemos enviar con ella cuando la devolvamos a su lugar».
es.R: Entonces los filisteos llamaron a sus sacerdotes y a los hombres que decían descubrir cosas ocultas por medio de señales. Les preguntaron: «¿Qué hacemos con el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}? {{plural_you:Dígannos|Decidnos}} qué debemos mandar junto con ella cuando la devolvamos a su lugar».

fr.L: Et les Philistins appelèrent les prêtres et les devins, en disant : « Que ferons-nous de l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ? Faites-nous savoir avec quoi nous la renverrons à sa place. »
fr.B: Les Philistins convoquèrent alors les prêtres et les devins et leur dirent : « Que devons-nous faire de l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ? Dites-nous ce que nous devons envoyer avec elle quand nous la renverrons chez elle. »
fr.R: Alors les Philistins ont appelé leurs prêtres et les hommes qui prétendaient découvrir les choses cachées grâce à des signes. Ils leur ont demandé : « Que devons-nous faire de l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ? Dites-nous ce que nous devons envoyer avec elle quand nous la renverrons là où elle doit être. »

sw.L: Na Wafilisti wakawaita makuhani na waaguzi, wakisema, "Tulifanye nini sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}? Tujulisheni tulirudishe mahali pake pamoja na nini."
sw.B: Ndipo Wafilisti wakawaita makuhani na waaguzi wakasema, "Tufanye nini na sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}? Tuambieni tulipeleke pamoja na nini tunapolirudisha mahali pake."
sw.R: Ndipo Wafilisti wakawaita makuhani wao na watu waliodai kujua mambo yaliyofichika kwa kusoma ishara. Wakawauliza, "Tufanye nini na sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}? Tuambieni tutume nini pamoja nalo tunapolirudisha mahali pake."

vi.L: Người Phi-li-tin gọi các thầy tế lễ và các thầy bói mà nói: "Chúng ta phải làm gì với hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}? Hãy cho chúng ta biết phải gửi hòm về chỗ của nó với vật gì."
vi.B: Người Phi-li-tin cho mời các thầy tế lễ và các thầy bói đến và hỏi: "Chúng ta phải làm gì với hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}? Hãy cho chúng ta biết phải gửi gì theo khi đưa hòm về chỗ của nó."
vi.R: Người Phi-li-tin cho gọi các thầy tế lễ của họ và những người tự cho là đọc được điều bí ẩn qua các điềm lạ. Họ hỏi: "Chúng ta phải làm gì với hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}? Hãy cho chúng ta biết phải gửi gì theo khi đưa hòm về nơi của nó."

ko.L: 그리고 블레셋 사람들이 제사장들과 점쟁이들을 불러 말했다. "우리가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 궤를 어떻게 해야 하겠소? 무엇과 함께 그것을 제자리로 보내야 할지 우리에게 알려 주시오."
ko.B: 블레셋 사람들이 제사장들과 점쟁이들을 불러 물었다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 궤를 어떻게 하면 좋겠소? 그것을 제자리로 돌려보낼 때 무엇을 함께 보내야 할지 알려 주시오."
ko.R: 블레셋 사람들은 자기들의 제사장들과, 징조를 보고 숨은 일을 알아낸다고 하는 사람들을 불렀다. 그들이 물었다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 궤를 어떻게 해야 하오? 그것을 원래 있던 곳으로 돌려보낼 때 무엇을 함께 보내야 할지 말해 주시오."

pt.L: E [os] filisteus chamaram os sacerdotes e os adivinhos, dizendo: "Que faremos com a arca {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}? Façam-nos saber com que a enviaremos ao seu lugar."
pt.B: Então os filisteus chamaram os sacerdotes e os adivinhos e disseram: "Que devemos fazer com a arca {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}? Digam-nos o que devemos mandar junto com ela quando a devolvermos ao seu lugar."
pt.R: Então os filisteus chamaram os seus sacerdotes e os homens que diziam descobrir coisas escondidas por meio de sinais. Eles perguntaram: "O que devemos fazer com a arca {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}? Digam para nós o que devemos mandar junto com ela quando a devolvermos para o lugar dela."

am.L: ፍልስጥኤማውያንም ካህናቱንና ሟርተኞቹን ጠርተው፦ «{{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ታቦት ምን እናድርግ? በምን አድርገን ወደ ስፍራው እንደምንሰድደው አስታውቁን» አሉ።
am.B: ከዚያም ፍልስጥኤማውያን ካህናቱንና ሟርተኞቹን አስጠርተው እንዲህ አሉ፦ «{{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ታቦት ምን እናድርግ? ወደ ስፍራው ስንመልሰው ከእርሱ ጋር ምን እንደምንልክ ንገሩን።»
am.R: ከዚያም ፍልስጥኤማውያን ካህናቶቻቸውንና ከምልክቶች የተሰወረውን ነገር እናውቃለን የሚሉትን ሰዎች ጠሩ። እንዲህም ብለው ጠየቋቸው፦ «{{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ታቦት ምን እናድርግ? ወደ ስፍራው ስንመልሰው ከእርሱ ጋር ምን መላክ እንዳለብን ንገሩን።»

decisions.choice: diviners: people who claimed to learn hidden things or the future from signs and omens
decisions.reason: Divination was common among Israel's neighbors and forbidden in Israel (Deuteronomy 18:10, 14). The Philistines call on their own religious experts to explain what has happened and what to do.

decisions.choice: with what: with what gift the ark should go back
alternatives: how shall we send it to its place?
decisions.reason: The question can mean "how" or "with what". The answer in verses 3-5, a guilt offering of gold sent along with the ark, shows that they are asking what should go with it.

decisions.choice: its place: the ark's own home among the Israelites
decisions.reason: The ark belonged with the people of the God of Israel, not in a Philistine temple (5:2-4, 11).

decisions.choice: the men who claimed to learn hidden things from signs
decisions.reason: Readable explains "diviners", a word many readers do not know, and says "their priests" because these are the Philistines' own priests.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Hágannos|Hacednos}}, {{plural_you:Dígannos|Decidnos}}
decisions.reason: The Philistines speak to the priests and diviners as a group, so the command takes the plural-you setting, as everywhere a group is addressed.

decisions.choice: waaguzi (L, B); watu waliodai kujua mambo yaliyofichika kwa kusoma ishara (R)
decisions.reason: "Mwaguzi" is one who divines hidden things from signs (m1), without the sense of witchcraft in "mchawi" or of healing in "mganga"; Readable explains it as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "các thầy bói" (L, B) for the diviners; Readable explains, as the English does
decisions.reason: People who claimed to read hidden things from signs (meaning decision); "thầy bói" is the everyday Vietnamese word for such a person.

decisions.choice: The Philistine leaders and their priests and diviners speak to each other in the semi-formal style (하오체)
decisions.reason: Men of standing consulting their own experts speak with mutual respect but not deference; 하오체 marks that.

decisions.choice: "징조를 보고 숨은 일을 알아낸다고 하는 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English Readable, Readable says what diviners claimed to do.

decisions.choice: os adivinhos
decisions.reason: "Adivinho" is the Portuguese word for one who reads omens (m1), as Deuteronomy 18:10, 14; "vidente" is kept for Samuel the seer (9:9). Readable explains the word, as the English does.

decisions.choice: diviners are "ሟርተኞች" at Literal and Balanced; Readable describes them, as the English does.
decisions.reason: "ሟርተኛ" is the Amharic word for one who reads omens and foretells; "ጠንቋይ" suggests spirit-possession, and "አስማተኞች" is kept for Exodus's magicians.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ אִֽם־מְשַׁלְּחִ֞ים אֶת־אֲר֨וֹן אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אַל־תְּשַׁלְּח֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ רֵיקָ֔ם כִּֽי־הָשֵׁ֥ב תָּשִׁ֛יבוּ ל֖וֹ אָשָׁ֑ם אָ֤ז תֵּרָֽפְאוּ֙ וְנוֹדַ֣ע לָכֶ֔ם לָ֛מָּה לֹא־תָס֥וּר יָד֖וֹ מִכֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said, If [you are] sending [the] ark of [the] God of Israel, do not send it empty, but surely return to him a guilt offering; then you will be healed, and it will be known to you why not turns aside his hand from you.

en.L: And they said, "If you [are] sending away the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it away empty, but you must surely return to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a guilt offering. Then you will be healed, and it will be known to you why {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand does not turn aside from you."
en.B: They answered, "If you are sending the ark of the God of Israel away, you must not send it empty. Be sure to return a guilt offering to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then you will be healed, and you will know why {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand has not been taken away from you."
en.R: They answered, "If you send away the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it back with nothing. You must send {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a guilt offering to make up for the wrong you have done. Then you will be healed, and you will know why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has kept on punishing you."

es.L: Y ellos dijeron: «Si {{plural_you:envían|enviáis}} el arca del Dios de Israel, no la {{plural_you:envíen|enviéis}} vacía, sino que sin falta {{plural_you:le devolverán|le devolveréis}} una ofrenda por la culpa. Entonces {{plural_you:serán sanados|seréis sanados}}, y {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} por qué no se aparta de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano».
es.B: Ellos respondieron: «Si {{plural_you:van|vais}} a devolver el arca del Dios de Israel, no la {{plural_you:devuelvan|devolváis}} con las manos vacías. {{plural_you:Asegúrense|Aseguraos}} de devolverle una ofrenda por la culpa. Entonces {{plural_you:sanarán|sanaréis}}, y {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} por qué {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano no se ha apartado de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}».
es.R: Ellos respondieron: «Si {{plural_you:devuelven|devolvéis}} el arca del Dios de Israel, no la {{plural_you:manden|mandéis}} sin nada. {{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} que enviarle una ofrenda por la culpa para reparar el mal que {{plural_you:han hecho|habéis hecho}}. Entonces {{plural_you:sanarán|sanaréis}}, y {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} por qué {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:los|os}} ha seguido castigando».

fr.L: Et ils dirent : « Si vous renvoyez l’arche du Dieu d’Israël, ne la renvoyez pas à vide, mais ne manquez pas de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rendre un sacrifice de réparation. Alors vous serez guéris, et vous saurez pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main ne se détourne pas de vous. »
fr.B: Ils répondirent : « Si vous renvoyez l’arche du Dieu d’Israël, ne la renvoyez pas les mains vides. Ne manquez pas de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} offrir un sacrifice de réparation. Alors vous serez guéris, et vous saurez pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main ne s’est pas retirée de vous. »
fr.R: Ils ont répondu : « Si vous renvoyez l’arche du Dieu d’Israël, ne la renvoyez pas sans rien. Vous devez {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} envoyer une offrande de réparation pour réparer le mal que vous avez fait. Alors vous serez guéris, et vous saurez pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a continué à vous punir. »

sw.L: Nao wakasema, "Kama mnalirudisha sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli, msilipeleke tupu, bali hakika mrudishieni sadaka ya hatia. Ndipo mtaponywa, na mtajulishwa kwa nini mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} haujaondoka kwenu."
sw.B: Wakajibu, "Ikiwa mnalirudisha sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli, msilirudishe mikono mitupu. Hakikisheni mnamrudishia sadaka ya hatia. Ndipo mtaponywa, nanyi mtajua kwa nini mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} haujaondolewa juu yenu."
sw.R: Wakajibu, "Mkilirudisha sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli, msilirudishe bila kitu. Lazima mmpelekee sadaka ya hatia ili kufidia kosa mlilofanya. Ndipo mtaponywa, nanyi mtajua kwa nini ameendelea kuwaadhibu."

decisions.choice: guilt offering: a payment that makes up for a wrong done
decisions.reason: The word is the name of the guilt offering in Leviticus 5:14-26, where someone who has wronged what is holy pays it back and adds more. The Philistines had taken what belonged to Israel's God, so they return the ark with a payment of gold (verses 4-5, 8).

decisions.choice: his hand does not turn aside: he keeps on striking you
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for God's power in action. In chapter 5 his hand was heavy on each city that held the ark (5:6, 7, 9, 11).

decisions.choice: you will know why his hand has not left you: once you are healed, it will be clear that his hand was the cause
alternatives: then you will be healed, and it will become known to you why his hand did not turn from you
and atonement will be made for you; will his hand not then turn from you?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short and can be read in more than one way. Read as it stands, healing after the offering will show that it was the God of Israel who had been striking them. The ancient Greek translation has "and atonement will be made for you; should not his hand then leave you?", which may reflect a different Hebrew text. The test in verse 9 takes up the same question of whether his hand was really the cause.

decisions.choice: a guilt offering to make up for the wrong you have done; he has kept on punishing you
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a guilt offering is for and says plainly what "his hand has not turned aside" means.

decisions.choice: "un sacrifice de réparation" (Literal, Balanced); "une offrande de réparation" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch note's term for the guilt offering, which says what it is for, making up for a wrong (m1). Here it is gold objects, not an animal, so Readable says "offrande".

decisions.choice: "una ofrenda por la culpa"
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch's term is "el sacrificio por la culpa"; here the Philistines' gift is gold objects, not an animal (m1), so the Spanish keeps the term's "por la culpa" with "ofrenda", the wider word.

decisions.choice: sadaka ya hatia
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch note: the guilt offering is "sadaka ya hatia"; Readable adds that it makes up for the wrong, as the English Readable does. "Him" and "he" sit inside the Swahili verbs and take no span; "wake" does.

decisions.choice: "lễ vật chuộc lỗi" for the guilt offering
decisions.reason: A payment that makes up for a wrong (meaning decision); "chuộc lỗi" keeps it apart from the sin offering. The Philistine priests call the Philistines "các ông" and speak of Israel's God as "vị thần ấy" at Balanced and Readable, as in 5:7.

decisions.choice: "속건제물"
decisions.reason: "속건제" is the established Korean name for the guilt offering of Leviticus 5; here it is a payment for the wrong done (m1).

decisions.choice: uma oferta pela culpa
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch's term for the guilt offering of Leviticus 5 (m1), kept at every level as the English keeps "guilt offering"; Readable adds what it is for. The priests and diviners speak to the Philistines with "vocês".

en.L: And they said, "What [is] the guilt offering that we shall return to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?" And they said, "[By the] number of the rulers of [the] Philistines, five tumors of gold and five rats of gold, for one plague [was] on all of them and on your rulers.
en.B: They asked, "What guilt offering should we return to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?" They answered, "Five gold tumors and five gold rats, one for each of the rulers of the Philistines, because the same plague struck all the people and your rulers.

es.B: Ellos preguntaron: «¿Qué ofrenda por la culpa {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} debemos devolver?». Les respondieron: «Cinco tumores de oro y cinco ratas de oro, una por cada uno de los jefes de los filisteos, porque la misma plaga cayó sobre todo el pueblo y sobre {{plural_you:sus jefes|vuestros jefes}}.
es.R: Los filisteos preguntaron: «¿Qué ofrenda por la culpa {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} debemos enviar?». Los sacerdotes y adivinos respondieron: «{{plural_you:Envíen|Enviad}} cinco tumores de oro y cinco ratas de oro, una por cada uno de los cinco jefes filisteos. La misma plaga ha caído sobre todo {{plural_you:su pueblo|vuestro pueblo}} y sobre {{plural_you:sus jefes|vuestros jefes}}.

Le même fléau a frappé tout votre peuple et vos princes.

am.L: እነርሱም፦ «የምንመልስለት የበደል መሥዋዕት ምንድን [ነው]?» አሉ። እነርሱም እንዲህ አሉ፦ «እንደ ፍልስጥኤማውያን ገዢዎች ቁጥር አምስት የወርቅ እባጮችና አምስት የወርቅ አይጦች፤ በሁላችሁና በገዢዎቻችሁ ላይ አንድ መቅሠፍት [ነበረ]ና።
am.B: እነርሱም፦ «የምንመልስለት የበደል መሥዋዕት ምንድን ነው?» ብለው ጠየቁ። እነርሱም እንዲህ ብለው መለሱ፦ «ለእያንዳንዱ የፍልስጥኤማውያን ገዢ አንድ አንድ፣ አምስት የወርቅ እባጮችና አምስት የወርቅ አይጦች ይሁኑ፤ ሕዝቡንም ሁሉ ገዢዎቻችሁንም የመታው አንድ መቅሠፍት ነውና።
am.R: ፍልስጥኤማውያንም፦ «የምንልክለት የበደል መሥዋዕት ምንድን ነው?» ብለው ጠየቁ። ካህናቱና ሟርተኞቹም እንዲህ ብለው መለሱ፦ «ለአምስቱ የፍልስጥኤማውያን ገዢዎች ለእያንዳንዳቸው አንድ አንድ፣ አምስት የወርቅ እባጮችና አምስት የወርቅ አይጦች ላኩ። ሕዝባችሁን ሁሉና ገዢዎቻችሁን የመታው ያው አንዱ መቅሠፍት ነው።

decisions.choice: rulers of the Philistines: the lords of the five Philistine cities
decisions.reason: This title is used only for the Philistine rulers. There were five of them, one each for Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron (verse 17; Joshua 13:3; Judges 3:3).

decisions.choice: tumors: swellings on the body
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text here, as in 5:6-12 and 6:5, has a word that means "mounds" or "swellings". The scribes' tradition for reading aloud replaces it with another word for tumors or swellings, perhaps a more polite one. Either way the plague caused painful swellings. What disease it was is not certain; some think of the swellings of bubonic plague, which rats spread, and the older word "emerods" (hemorrhoids) reflects another guess.

decisions.choice: rats: rodents that were ruining the land (verse 5)
decisions.reason: The word names a small rodent, a mouse or a rat; the language does not separate the two. Since these creatures were destroying the land (verse 5) and the plague brought swellings, a rat plague is likely, but the word itself does not settle which animal is meant.

decisions.choice: all of them and your rulers: the whole people and their rulers alike
decisions.reason: The speakers shift from "them" to "your". "All of them" is the Philistine people, and the same plague struck the rulers too, so each ruler sends an offering for his city.

decisions.choice: one for each of the rulers; all the people
decisions.reason: "The number of the rulers" means one gold image for each ruler, which Balanced and Readable say plainly. Both say "the people" for "all of them", and Readable names who is speaking in each half of the verse.

decisions.choice: "chuột" for the rodents
decisions.reason: The general Vietnamese word for rats and mice, as the meaning decision leaves the kind open.

decisions.choice: ratos
decisions.reason: Portuguese "rato" covers both the mouse and the rat, as the Hebrew word does (m3), so it needs no choice between them; "camundongo" would decide for the mouse.

source.text: וַעֲשִׂיתֶם֩ צַלְמֵ֨י טְחֹרֵיכֶ֜ם וְצַלְמֵ֣י עַכְבְּרֵיכֶ֗ם הַמַּשְׁחִיתִם֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וּנְתַתֶּ֛ם לֵאלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כָּב֑וֹד אוּלַ֗י יָקֵ֤ל אֶת־יָדוֹ֙ מֵֽעֲלֵיכֶ֔ם וּמֵעַ֥ל אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם וּמֵעַ֥ל אַרְצְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make images of your tumors and images of your mice that are ruining the land, and you will give to [the] God of Israel glory; perhaps he will lighten his hand from on you and from on your gods and from on your land.

en.L: And you will make images of your tumors and images of your rats that are ruining the land, and you will give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will lighten {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand from on you and from on your gods and from on your land.
en.B: So make images of your tumors and images of your rats that are destroying the land, and give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will lighten {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand on you, on your gods and on your land.
en.R: Make gold models of your tumors and of the rats that are ruining your land. In this way, give honor to the God of Israel. Then perhaps {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will stop punishing you and your gods and your land so heavily.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:harán|haréis}} imágenes de {{plural_you:sus tumores|vuestros tumores}} e imágenes de {{plural_you:sus ratas|vuestras ratas}} que destruyen la tierra, y {{plural_you:darán|daréis}} gloria al Dios de Israel. Quizá aligere {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano de sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y de sobre {{plural_you:sus dioses|vuestros dioses}}, y de sobre {{plural_you:su tierra|vuestra tierra}}.
es.B: Así que {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} imágenes de {{plural_you:sus tumores|vuestros tumores}} y de las ratas que están destruyendo la tierra, y {{plural_you:den|dad}} gloria al Dios de Israel. Quizá aligere {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, sobre {{plural_you:sus dioses|vuestros dioses}} y sobre {{plural_you:su tierra|vuestra tierra}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} figuras de oro de {{plural_you:sus tumores|vuestros tumores}} y de las ratas que están arruinando {{plural_you:su tierra|vuestra tierra}}. De ese modo {{plural_you:honren|honrad}} al Dios de Israel. Quizá así deje de {{plural_you:castigarlos|castigaros}} tan duramente a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, a {{plural_you:sus dioses|vuestros dioses}} y a {{plural_you:su tierra|vuestra tierra}}.

fr.L: Et vous ferez des images de vos tumeurs et des images de vos rats qui ravagent le pays, et vous donnerez gloire au Dieu d’Israël. Peut-être {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} allégera {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main de dessus vous, et de dessus vos dieux, et de dessus votre pays.
fr.B: Faites donc des images de vos tumeurs et des images des rats qui dévastent le pays, et rendez gloire au Dieu d’Israël. Peut-être allégera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main qui pèse sur vous, sur vos dieux et sur votre pays.
fr.R: Faites des modèles en or de vos tumeurs et des rats qui ravagent votre pays. Ainsi, vous rendrez honneur au Dieu d’Israël. Alors peut-être qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} arrêtera de vous punir si durement, vous, vos dieux et votre pays.

sw.L: Nanyi mtatengeneza sanamu za majipu yenu na sanamu za panya wenu wanaoiharibu nchi, nanyi mtampa Mungu wa Israeli utukufu. Huenda atapunguza uzito wa mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} juu yenu na juu ya miungu yenu na juu ya nchi yenu.
sw.B: Basi tengenezeni sanamu za majipu yenu na sanamu za panya wenu wanaoiharibu nchi, mkampe Mungu wa Israeli utukufu. Huenda atapunguza uzito wa mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} juu yenu, juu ya miungu yenu na juu ya nchi yenu.
sw.R: Tengenezeni mifano ya dhahabu ya majipu yenu na ya panya wanaoiharibu nchi yenu. Kwa njia hiyo mpeni Mungu wa Israeli heshima. Huenda ataacha kuwaadhibu kwa ukali hivyo, ninyi na miungu yenu na nchi yenu.

vi.L: Các ông hãy làm hình các cái bướu của các ông và hình các con chuột đang phá hại xứ, và dâng vinh quang cho Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên. Biết đâu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ làm nhẹ tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên các ông, trên các thần của các ông và trên xứ các ông.
vi.B: Vậy hãy làm hình các cái bướu và hình những con chuột đang phá hoại xứ sở các ông, và tôn vinh Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên. Biết đâu vị thần ấy sẽ nhẹ tay với các ông, với các thần của các ông và với xứ các ông.
vi.R: Hãy làm mô hình bằng vàng của các cái bướu và của những con chuột đang phá hại xứ các ông. Làm như vậy là tôn vinh Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên. Biết đâu vị thần ấy sẽ thôi trừng phạt nặng nề các ông, các thần của các ông và xứ các ông.

ko.L: 그리고 여러분의 종기의 형상과 땅을 망치는 여러분의 쥐들의 형상을 만들어 이스라엘의 하나님께 영광을 돌리시오. 혹시 그가 여러분과 여러분의 신들과 여러분의 땅 위에서 그의 손을 가볍게 할지도 모르오.
ko.B: 그러니 여러분의 종기 모양과 땅을 망치는 쥐 모양을 만들어 이스라엘의 하나님께 영광을 돌리시오. 그러면 혹시 그가 여러분과 여러분의 신들과 여러분의 땅을 누르던 손을 가볍게 할지도 모르오.
ko.R: 여러분의 종기와 여러분의 땅을 망치는 쥐들을 금으로 본떠 만드시오. 그렇게 해서 이스라엘의 하나님께 영광을 돌리시오. 그러면 그가 여러분과 여러분의 신들과 여러분의 땅을 그렇게 심하게 벌하지 않을지도 모르오.

pt.L: E vocês farão imagens dos seus tumores e imagens dos seus ratos que estão arruinando a terra, e darão glória ao Deus de Israel. Talvez {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} alivie a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão de sobre vocês, e de sobre os seus deuses, e de sobre a sua terra.
pt.B: Façam, então, imagens dos seus tumores e imagens dos ratos que estão destruindo a terra, e deem glória ao Deus de Israel. Talvez {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} alivie o peso da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão sobre vocês, sobre os seus deuses e sobre a sua terra.
pt.R: Façam modelos de ouro dos seus tumores e dos ratos que estão acabando com a terra de vocês. Assim vocês vão honrar o Deus de Israel. Então talvez {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} pare de castigar com tanta força vocês, os seus deuses e a sua terra.

am.L: ምድሪቱን የሚያጠፉትን የእባጮቻችሁንና የአይጦቻችሁን ምስሎች ትሠራላችሁ፤ ለእስራኤልም አምላክ ክብርን ትሰጣላችሁ፤ ምናልባት ከእናንተና ከአማልክታችሁ ከምድራችሁም ላይ እጁን ያቀልል ይሆናል።
am.B: ስለዚህ የእባጮቻችሁንና ምድሪቱን የሚያጠፉትን የአይጦቻችሁን ምስሎች ሥሩ፤ ለእስራኤልም አምላክ ክብርን ስጡ። ምናልባት በእናንተ፣ በአማልክታችሁና በምድራችሁ ላይ ያከበደውን እጁን ያቀልል ይሆናል።
am.R: የእባጮቻችሁንና ምድራችሁን የሚያጠፉትን የአይጦችን ምስሎች ከወርቅ ሥሩ። በዚህም ለእስራኤል አምላክ ክብር ስጡ። ምናልባት በእናንተ፣ በአማልክታችሁና በምድራችሁ ላይ የሚያመጣውን ከባድ ቅጣት ያቆም ይሆናል።

decisions.choice: the rats that are ruining the land: rodents swarming over Philistine country
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text of chapter 5 speaks only of tumors; the rats appear for the first time here, as if the reader already knows of them. The ancient Greek translation mentions mice spreading through the land already in 5:6 and 6:1.

decisions.choice: give glory to the God of Israel: openly admit his power and that he has been wronged
decisions.reason: To give glory to God can mean to confess the truth before him (Joshua 7:19). The gold images admit that the plague came from him. The word "glory" is related to "heavy": his hand was heavy on them (5:6, 11), and now they honor him so that he will make it light.

decisions.choice: lighten his hand: ease the punishment
decisions.reason: The picture of a heavy hand pressing down on someone (5:6, 11) is turned around: they hope he will lift its weight.

decisions.choice: your gods: the Philistine gods, Dagon among them
decisions.reason: Dagon's image had fallen and broken before the ark (5:2-5), so the speakers count their own gods among those struck.

decisions.choice: gold models; honor
decisions.reason: Readable says "models" for "images" and adds that they are gold, as verse 4 says. It uses "honor" for "glory", which here means showing respect.

source.text: וְלָ֤מָּה תְכַבְּדוּ֙ אֶת־לְבַבְכֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר כִּבְּד֛וּ מִצְרַ֥יִם וּפַרְעֹ֖ה אֶת־לִבָּ֑ם הֲלוֹא֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר הִתְעַלֵּ֣ל בָּהֶ֔ם וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֖וּם וַיֵּלֵֽכוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And why will you make heavy your heart as made heavy Egypt and Pharaoh their heart? Was it not when he dealt harshly with them, and they sent them away, and they went?

en.L: And why will you make your heart heavy, just as Egypt and Pharaoh made their heart heavy? Was it not when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had dealt harshly with them that they sent them away, and they went?
en.B: Why harden your hearts the way the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened theirs? Once {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had dealt harshly with them, did they not let the Israelites go, and they left?
en.R: Do not be stubborn the way the Egyptians and Pharaoh were. After God had punished them severely, they let the Israelites go, and the Israelites left Egypt.

es.L: ¿Y por qué {{plural_you:endurecerán|endureceréis}} {{plural_you:su corazón|vuestro corazón}}, como Egipto y el faraón endurecieron su corazón? ¿No fue cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los trató con dureza que los dejaron ir, y se fueron?
es.B: ¿Por qué {{plural_you:endurecer su corazón|endurecer vuestro corazón}} como lo endurecieron los egipcios y el faraón? Después de que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los trató con dureza, ¿no dejaron ir a los israelitas, y estos se fueron?
es.R: No {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} tercos como lo fueron los egipcios y el faraón. Después de que Dios los castigó duramente, dejaron ir a los israelitas, y los israelitas salieron de Egipto.

fr.L: Et pourquoi endurciriez-vous votre cœur comme l’Égypte et Pharaon ont endurci leur cœur ? N’est-ce pas quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les eut maltraités qu’ils les laissèrent partir, et ils s’en allèrent ?
fr.B: Pourquoi endurcir votre cœur comme les Égyptiens et Pharaon ont endurci le leur ? Après qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les eut durement traités, n’ont-ils pas laissé partir les Israélites, qui s’en sont allés ?
fr.R: Ne soyez pas têtus comme les Égyptiens et Pharaon. Quand Dieu les a durement punis, ils ont laissé partir les Israélites, et les Israélites ont quitté l’Égypte.

sw.L: Na kwa nini mnaifanya mioyo yenu kuwa mizito, kama Wamisri na Farao walivyoifanya mioyo yao kuwa mizito? Je, si alipokwisha kuwatendea kwa ukali ndipo walipowaacha waende, nao wakaenda?
sw.B: Kwa nini kuifanya mioyo yenu migumu kama Wamisri na Farao walivyoifanya yao? Alipokwisha kuwatendea kwa ukali, je, hawakuwaacha Waisraeli waende, nao wakaondoka?
sw.R: Msiwe wakaidi kama Wamisri na Farao walivyokuwa. Baada ya Mungu kuwaadhibu vikali, waliwaacha Waisraeli waende, nao Waisraeli wakaondoka Misri.

vi.L: Sao các ông lại làm cho lòng mình cứng cỏi như người Ai Cập và Pha-ra-ôn đã làm cho lòng họ cứng cỏi? Chẳng phải khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đối xử khắc nghiệt với họ, thì họ mới để dân ấy đi, và dân ấy đã ra đi sao?
vi.B: Sao các ông lại cứng lòng như người Ai Cập và Pha-ra-ôn đã cứng lòng? Khi vị thần ấy đã đối xử khắc nghiệt với họ, chẳng phải họ đã để dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đi, và dân ấy đã ra đi sao?
vi.R: Đừng cứng đầu như người Ai Cập và Pha-ra-ôn. Sau khi Đức Chúa Trời trừng phạt họ nặng nề, họ đã để dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đi, và dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã rời khỏi Ai Cập.

ko.L: 그리고 어찌하여 여러분은 이집트와 바로가 자기들의 마음을 무겁게 한 것처럼 여러분의 마음을 무겁게 하려 하오? 그가 그들을 혹독하게 다룬 뒤에야 그들이 그들을 보내어 그들이 가지 않았소?
ko.B: 어찌하여 이집트 사람들과 바로가 마음을 완고하게 했던 것처럼 여러분도 마음을 완고하게 하려 하오? 그가 그들을 혹독하게 다루자 그들이 이스라엘 사람들을 내보냈고, 이스라엘 사람들이 떠나가지 않았소?
ko.R: 이집트 사람들과 바로처럼 고집을 부리지 마시오. 하나님이 그들을 혹독하게 벌하자, 그들은 이스라엘 사람들을 내보냈고, 이스라엘 사람들은 이집트를 떠났소.

pt.L: E por que vocês endureceriam o seu coração, assim como o Egito e Faraó endureceram o seu coração? Não foi quando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os tratou com dureza que os deixaram ir, e eles se foram?
pt.B: Por que vocês endureceriam o coração, como os egípcios e Faraó endureceram o deles? Depois que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os tratou com dureza, não deixaram os israelitas partir, e eles se foram?
pt.R: Não sejam teimosos como os egípcios e Faraó foram. Depois que Deus os castigou duramente, eles deixaram os israelitas ir embora, e os israelitas saíram do Egito.

am.L: ግብፃውያንና ፈርዖን ልባቸውን እንዳከበዱ ለምን ልባችሁን ታከብዳላችሁ? እርሱ በተሳለቀባቸው ጊዜ አልለቀቋቸውምን? እነርሱም ሄዱ።
am.B: ግብፃውያንና ፈርዖን ልባቸውን እንዳደነደኑ እናንተ ለምን ልባችሁን ታደነድናላችሁ? እርሱ ክፉኛ ከቀጣቸው በኋላ እስራኤላውያንን አልለቀቋቸውምን? እነርሱም ሄዱ።
am.R: ግብፃውያንና ፈርዖን እንዳደረጉት እልከኞች አትሁኑ። እግዚአብሔር ክፉኛ ከቀጣቸው በኋላ እስራኤላውያንን ለቀቋቸው፤ እስራኤላውያንም ከግብፅ ወጡ።

decisions.choice: make your heart heavy: refuse to give in, as Pharaoh did
decisions.reason: The words recall the plagues in Egypt, where Pharaoh made his heart heavy and would not let Israel go (Exodus 8:11, 28; 9:34). The Philistines already knew that this God had struck Egypt (4:8). "Heavy" also ties in with the heavy hand of God (5:6, 11) and the glory of verse 5.

decisions.choice: dealt harshly: made sport of them, made them look foolish by his power
decisions.reason: The same verb is used when Yahweh tells how he dealt with Egypt (Exodus 10:2). It means to act against someone at will, showing them up as powerless.

decisions.choice: they sent them away, and they went: the Egyptians let the Israelites go
decisions.reason: The first "they" is the Egyptians and the second "them" is Israel, as in the Exodus story (Exodus 12:31-33).

decisions.choice: the Israelites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Israelites so that the pronouns are clear. Readable also gives "God" for "he" and turns the speaker's questions into plain statements, which say the same thing.

decisions.choice: "endurcir votre cœur"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "make your heart heavy", the words used of Pharaoh in Exodus (m1). French "endurcir le cœur" is the established phrase for Pharaoh's refusal and says what the Hebrew means; "appesantir" is understood only by those who know the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: mioyo mizito (L); mioyo migumu (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "heavy" heart; Balanced uses "moyo mgumu", the Swahili idiom for a stubborn heart, as the English says "harden".

decisions.choice: "làm cho lòng mình cứng cỏi" (L); "cứng lòng" (B); "cứng đầu" (R) for "make your heart heavy"
decisions.reason: Refusing to give in, as Pharaoh did (meaning decision); "cứng lòng" is the Vietnamese idiom for that stubbornness, and Readable uses the everyday "cứng đầu".

decisions.choice: The Philistine priests speak of Israel's God as "그" and "하나님" without the honorific "-시-"
decisions.reason: As 5:7: the honorific belongs to the narrator's and Israel's speech, not to the Philistines'.

decisions.choice: endurecer o coração
decisions.reason: "Make the heart heavy" is the expression of the Exodus plagues (m1); Portuguese says it as "endurecer o coração", as the Pentateuch's Portuguese does for Pharaoh, so Literal too uses the familiar phrase rather than "pesado", which in Portuguese suggests sadness.

decisions.choice: "make your heart heavy" (kabed) is "ልባችሁን ታከብዳላችሁ" at Literal, "ታደነድናላችሁ" at Balanced and "እልከኞች አትሁኑ" at Readable.
decisions.reason: The priests recall Exodus, so the verb follows the Pentateuch's rule for Pharaoh's heart: Literal keeps kabed as "አከበደ", Balanced "አደነደነ", Readable "እልከኛ".

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה קְח֨וּ וַעֲשׂ֜וּ עֲגָלָ֤ה חֲדָשָׁה֙ אֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּ֤י פָרוֹת֙ עָל֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־עָלָ֥ה עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם עֹ֑ל וַאֲסַרְתֶּ֤ם אֶת־הַפָּרוֹת֙ בָּעֲגָלָ֔ה וַהֲשֵׁיבֹתֶ֧ם בְּנֵיהֶ֛ם מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶ֖ם הַבָּֽיְתָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And now take and make one new cart and two nursing cows on which not has come up a yoke, and harness the cows to the cart, and take back their young from after them home.

en.L: And now take and prepare one new cart and two nursing cows on which no yoke has come, and harness the cows to the cart, and take their calves back home from behind them.
en.B: Now then, get a new cart ready, and two cows that are nursing calves and have never been yoked. Harness the cows to the cart, but take their calves away from them and back home.
en.R: So get a new cart ready. Find two cows that are nursing calves and have never pulled a load. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take their calves home, away from their mothers.

es.L: Y ahora {{plural_you:tomen|tomad}} y {{plural_you:preparen|preparad}} una carreta nueva y dos vacas que estén criando, sobre las cuales no haya subido yugo, y {{plural_you:unzan|uncid}} las vacas a la carreta, y {{plural_you:lleven|llevad}} sus becerros de detrás de ellas a casa.
es.B: Ahora, pues, {{plural_you:preparen|preparad}} una carreta nueva y dos vacas que estén criando y que nunca hayan llevado yugo. {{plural_you:Unzan|Uncid}} las vacas a la carreta, pero {{plural_you:quítenles|quitadles}} los becerros y {{plural_you:llévenlos|llevadlos}} a casa.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:preparen|preparad}} una carreta nueva. {{plural_you:Busquen|Buscad}} dos vacas que estén criando y que nunca hayan tirado de una carga. {{plural_you:Engánchenlas|Enganchadlas}} a la carreta, pero {{plural_you:lleven|llevad}} los becerros a casa, lejos de sus madres.

fr.L: Et maintenant, prenez et préparez un chariot neuf et deux vaches qui allaitent, sur lesquelles le joug n’est pas venu, et attelez les vaches au chariot, et ramenez à la maison leurs petits, loin d’elles.
fr.B: Maintenant donc, préparez un chariot neuf et deux vaches qui allaitent et qui n’ont jamais porté le joug. Attelez les vaches au chariot, mais ramenez leurs veaux à l’étable, loin d’elles.
fr.R: Alors, préparez un chariot neuf. Trouvez deux vaches qui allaitent leurs veaux et qui n’ont jamais tiré de charge. Attelez les vaches au chariot, mais ramenez leurs veaux à la maison, loin de leurs mères.

sw.L: Basi sasa chukueni mtengeneze gari moja jipya na ng'ombe wawili wanaonyonyesha ambao nira haijawahi kuwapanda, mkawafunge ng'ombe hao kwenye gari, na ndama wao mwarudishe nyumbani wasiwafuate.
sw.B: Basi sasa, andaeni gari jipya na ng'ombe wawili wanaonyonyesha ndama ambao hawajawahi kufungwa nira. Wafungeni ng'ombe hao kwenye gari, lakini ndama wao mwaondoe kwao mwarudishe nyumbani.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo andaeni gari jipya. Tafuteni ng'ombe wawili wanaonyonyesha ndama ambao hawajawahi kuvuta mzigo. Wafungeni ng'ombe hao kwenye gari, lakini ndama wao wapelekeni nyumbani, mbali na mama zao.

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ hãy lấy và làm một cỗ xe mới, và hai con bò cái đang cho con bú chưa hề mang ách; hãy thắng hai con bò cái vào xe, còn bê con của chúng thì đem về nhà, xa khỏi chúng.
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ hãy chuẩn bị một cỗ xe mới và hai con bò cái đang nuôi con, chưa hề mang ách. Hãy thắng hai bò cái vào xe, nhưng đem bê con của chúng về nhà.
vi.R: Vậy hãy chuẩn bị một cỗ xe mới. Hãy tìm hai con bò cái đang nuôi con và chưa hề kéo xe. Hãy thắng hai bò mẹ vào xe, còn bê con thì đem về nhà, xa bò mẹ.

ko.L: 그러니 이제 새 수레 하나와, 멍에를 메어 본 적이 없는 젖 나는 암소 두 마리를 가져다 마련하시오. 그리고 그 암소들을 수레에 매고, 그 송아지들은 어미들 뒤에서 떼어 집으로 돌려보내시오.
ko.B: 그러니 이제 새 수레 하나를 마련하고, 송아지에게 젖을 먹이고 있으면서 아직 멍에를 메어 본 적이 없는 암소 두 마리를 끌어오시오. 암소들은 수레에 매고, 송아지들은 어미에게서 떼어 집으로 데려가시오.
ko.R: 그러니 새 수레 하나를 마련하시오. 그리고 송아지에게 젖을 먹이고 있는 암소 두 마리를 찾으시오. 한 번도 짐을 끌어 본 적이 없는 소여야 하오. 암소들을 수레에 매고, 송아지들은 어미에게서 떼어 집으로 데려가시오.

pt.L: E agora tomem e preparem uma carroça nova e duas vacas que estejam amamentando, sobre as quais não tenha vindo jugo, e atrelem as vacas à carroça, e levem os seus bezerros de volta para casa, [tirando-os] de trás delas.
pt.B: Agora, então, preparem uma carroça nova e duas vacas que estejam amamentando bezerros e que nunca tenham levado jugo. Atrelem as vacas à carroça, mas tirem delas os bezerros e levem-nos de volta para casa.
pt.R: Então preparem uma carroça nova. Arranjem duas vacas que estejam amamentando bezerros e que nunca tenham puxado carga. Atrelem as vacas à carroça, mas levem os bezerros para casa, longe das mães.

am.L: አሁንም አንድ አዲስ ጋሪ ወስዳችሁ አዘጋጁ፤ ቀንበርም ያልተጫነባቸውን ሁለት የሚያጠቡ ላሞች [ውሰዱ]፤ ላሞቹንም በጋሪው ጥመዷቸው፤ ጥጆቻቸውንም ከኋላቸው ወደ ቤት መልሷቸው።
am.B: እንግዲህ አዲስ ጋሪና ጥጃ የሚያጠቡ፣ ቀንበርም ተጭኖባቸው የማያውቁ ሁለት ላሞች አዘጋጁ። ላሞቹን በጋሪው ጥመዷቸው፤ ጥጆቻቸውን ግን ከእነርሱ ለይታችሁ ወደ ቤት መልሷቸው።
am.R: ስለዚህ አዲስ ጋሪ አዘጋጁ። ጥጃ የሚያጠቡና ከዚህ በፊት ምንም ነገር ስበው የማያውቁ ሁለት ላሞች ፈልጉ። ላሞቹን በጋሪው ጥመዷቸው፤ ጥጆቻቸውን ግን ከእናቶቻቸው ለይታችሁ ወደ ቤት ውሰዷቸው።

decisions.choice: a new cart and cows never yoked: things not used before, fit for a holy purpose
decisions.reason: Animals that had never borne a yoke were set apart for special rites in Israel (Numbers 19:2; Deuteronomy 21:3). Unused things were fitting for carrying the ark.

decisions.choice: nursing cows whose calves are taken away: cows that will naturally want to go back to their calves
decisions.reason: Cows that had never been yoked would not pull together well, and cows separated from their calves would turn back toward them. If they went straight away from home instead, it would be a sign (verse 9).

decisions.choice: never pulled a load
decisions.reason: Readable explains being yoked by what it means for the cows.

decisions.choice: the cart is "ጋሪ"; the box (verse 8) "ሣጥን"; the rats "አይጦች".
decisions.reason: "ሠረገላ" is a chariot or carriage; a farm cart drawn by cows is a ጋሪ.

source.text: וּלְקַחְתֶּ֞ם אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֗ה וּנְתַתֶּ֤ם אֹתוֹ֙ אֶל־הָ֣עֲגָלָ֔ה וְאֵ֣ת׀כְּלֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֗ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֲשֵׁבֹתֶ֥ם לוֹ֙ אָשָׁ֔ם תָּשִׂ֥ימוּ בָאַרְגַּ֖ז מִצִּדּ֑וֹ וְשִׁלַּחְתֶּ֥ם אֹת֖וֹ וְהָלָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And take [the] ark of Yahweh and put it on the cart, and the articles of gold which you are returning to him [as] a guilt offering put in a box at its side; and send it away, and it will go.

en.L: And take the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and put it on the cart, and the articles of gold that you are returning to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [as] a guilt offering, put [them] in a box at its side. And send it away, and it will go.
en.B: Take the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and set it on the cart, and put the gold objects that you are returning to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as a guilt offering in a box beside it. Then send it off and let it go its way.
en.R: Put the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the cart. Put the gold objects in a box beside it. They are your guilt offering to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then send the cart off and let it go on its own.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:tomen|tomad}} el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y {{plural_you:pónganla|ponedla}} sobre la carreta, y los objetos de oro que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} {{plural_you:devuelven|devolvéis}} [como] ofrenda por la culpa, {{plural_you:pónganlos|ponedlos}} en una caja a su lado. Y {{plural_you:déjenla|dejadla}} ir, y se irá.
es.B: {{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}} el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y {{plural_you:colóquenla|colocadla}} sobre la carreta, y {{plural_you:pongan|poned}} en una caja, a su lado, los objetos de oro que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} {{plural_you:devuelven|devolvéis}} como ofrenda por la culpa. Luego {{plural_you:déjenla|dejadla}} partir y que siga su camino.
es.R: {{plural_you:Pongan|Poned}} el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} sobre la carreta. {{plural_you:Pongan|Poned}} los objetos de oro en una caja junto a ella. Son {{plural_you:su ofrenda|vuestra ofrenda}} por la culpa para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Luego {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} que la carreta se vaya sola.

fr.L: Et prenez l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et mettez-la sur le chariot ; et les objets d’or que vous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rendez [comme] sacrifice de réparation, mettez-[les] dans un coffret à son côté. Et renvoyez-la, et elle s’en ira.
fr.B: Prenez l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et placez-la sur le chariot ; mettez à côté d’elle, dans un coffret, les objets d’or que vous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rendez comme sacrifice de réparation. Puis laissez-la partir, et qu’elle s’en aille.
fr.R: Mettez l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} sur le chariot. Mettez les objets en or dans un coffret, à côté d’elle. C’est votre offrande de réparation pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Puis laissez le chariot partir tout seul.

sw.L: Na chukueni sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} mkaliweke juu ya gari, na vitu vya dhahabu mnavyomrudishia [kuwa] sadaka ya hatia, viwekeni katika kasha kando yake. Kisha lipelekeni, nalo litakwenda.
sw.B: Chukueni sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} mkaliweke juu ya gari, na vitu vya dhahabu mnavyomrudishia kama sadaka ya hatia viwekeni katika kasha kando yake. Kisha liacheni liende zake.
sw.R: Wekeni sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} juu ya gari. Wekeni vitu vya dhahabu katika kasha kando yake. Hivyo ndivyo sadaka yenu ya hatia kwake. Kisha liacheni gari liende lenyewe.

vi.L: Hãy lấy hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đặt lên xe, còn các vật bằng vàng mà các ông trả lại cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [làm] lễ vật chuộc lỗi thì đặt [chúng] trong một cái rương bên cạnh hòm. Rồi hãy cho xe đi, và nó sẽ đi.
vi.B: Hãy lấy hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đặt lên xe, và bỏ các vật bằng vàng mà các ông trả lại cho vị thần ấy làm lễ vật chuộc lỗi vào một cái rương bên cạnh. Rồi hãy cho xe đi theo đường của nó.
vi.R: Hãy đặt hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} lên xe. Hãy bỏ các vật bằng vàng vào một cái rương bên cạnh hòm. Đó là lễ vật chuộc lỗi của các ông dâng cho vị thần ấy. Rồi hãy cho xe tự đi.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 궤를 가져다 수레에 싣고, 속건제물로 그에게 돌려 드리는 금 물건들은 상자에 넣어 그 곁에 두시오. 그리고 그것을 보내어 가게 하시오.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 궤를 수레에 싣고, 속건제물로 그에게 돌려 드릴 금 물건들은 상자에 담아 궤 곁에 두시오. 그리고 수레를 보내어 제 길로 가게 하시오.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 궤를 수레에 실으시오. 금으로 만든 물건들은 상자에 담아 궤 옆에 두시오. 그것은 그에게 드리는 속건제물이오. 그리고 수레를 떠나보내어 저절로 가게 하시오.

pt.L: E tomem a arca {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e ponham-na na carroça, e os objetos de ouro que vocês {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} estão devolvendo [como] oferta pela culpa, ponham[-nos] numa caixa ao lado dela. E mandem-na embora, e ela irá.
pt.B: Peguem a arca {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e coloquem-na na carroça, e ponham numa caixa ao lado dela os objetos de ouro que vocês {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} estão devolvendo como oferta pela culpa. Depois mandem a carroça embora e deixem que ela siga o seu caminho.
pt.R: Coloquem a arca {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} na carroça. Ponham os objetos de ouro numa caixa ao lado dela. Eles são a oferta pela culpa que vocês vão dar a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}. Depois mandem a carroça embora e deixem que ela vá sozinha.

am.L: {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ታቦትም ወስዳችሁ በጋሪው ላይ አኑሩት፤ የበደል መሥዋዕት አድርጋችሁ የምትመልሱለትንም የወርቅ ዕቃዎች በአጠገቡ በሣጥን ውስጥ አኑሩ፤ ስደዱትም፤ ይሄዳልም።
